bullets.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5.29–5.30%, multi-decade high; real rates near GFC levels
bullets.body: The US 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.29–5.30%, the highest level since 2007, driven by investor concerns over rising deficits, heavy bond issuance, AI-related corporate borrowing, and structural long-term demand weakness. Citadel Securities attributes the spike to Fed policy stance, not just inflation. Real 30-year rates (per Barclays) are now approaching levels last seen at the 2008 GFC onset, and the 2s10s spread has steepened +25bps off July lows. UK 30y gilts hit 5.81% (highest since mid-May), German 10y at 3.21% (14-year high), and French 10y and 30y yields at multi-decade highs simultaneously.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo revises Fed call to +25bps hike in 2026; Goldman says September hike very unlikely
bullets.body: Wells Fargo Investment Institute reversed its prior no-change forecast, now expecting a 25bp hike in 2026 and another in 2027, lifting fed funds to 4.00–4.25%. Goldman Sachs, in contrast, says a September hike is very unlikely given weaker jobs, inflation, and consumer data, though prediction markets still price 49% odds of a hike before 2027. An SF Fed economist separately estimated the medium-run neutral rate at ~1.5%, implying current policy is accommodative assuming 2.5%+ inflation.

bullets.title: Empire Manufacturing beats big (20.6 vs 10.0 est); new orders and shipments fell
bullets.body: The August Empire Manufacturing Index surged to 20.6 vs. 10.0 estimate and 15.6 prior, but the internals were softer: new orders dropped to 17.3 from 22.2, shipments fell to 11.7 from 24.4, employment dipped to 9.3, and prices paid accelerated to 58.6 from 52.3. NY manufacturing index separately hit a 4-year high with employment rising but supply chains tightening.

bullets.title: NAHB housing index beats (35 vs 33 est) but remains deeply depressed; 30y rates threaten housing
bullets.body: August NAHB Housing Market Index came in at 35, above the 33 consensus and 34 prior, though the level remains historically weak. With real 30-year rates near GFC levels and nominal 30y yields at 5.29%, the housing market faces significant structural headwinds from elevated financing costs.

bullets.title: Evercore sees S&P 500 at 9,000 in 12 months; Goldman flags Q2 revenue at 5-year high
bullets.body: Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel targets S&P 500 at 9,000 within 12 months (~16% upside), citing the absence of traditional bull-market killers. Goldman Sachs separately reported S&P 500 revenues grew 6.4% YoY in Q2 ex-energy, the fastest in five years, with corporate earnings jumping nearly 50% YoY—though median ex-tech revenue rose only 3%, underscoring tech concentration. The top 10 S&P 500 companies' forward P/E has converged to the rest of the index, reducing their valuation premium.

bullets.title: BTIG warns seasonal pullback risk; ECB and Dalio flag AI-driven bubble conditions
bullets.body: BTIG warns US stocks are entering the historically weakest period of midterm election years, with valuations stretched and VIX near 2026 lows; since 1990 the equal-weight S&P 500 has typically suffered at least a 7% decline in this window. The ECB warns AI-driven tech valuations are approaching dot-com bubble levels with less fiscal/monetary room to respond than in 2000. Ray Dalio separately called out classic bubble signs in AI, comparing current market to 1929 and 2000 peaks.

bullets.title: SPX 0DTE implied vol at near-record lows; $11.7M VIX call bet and record speculator shorts vs. 15-year high insider buying
bullets.body: SPX 7790 0DTE straddle is pricing just 29bps—near Christmas Eve 2025 lows despite an average daily realized move of 68bps—signaling extreme complacency. Separately, someone purchased $11.7M in far-OTM VIX calls expiring in one month, and traders are at record short levels while corporate insiders are near 15-year highs in buying activity, creating a notable contrarian divergence.

bullets.title: Goldman One-Delta: stay risk-on, dump bonds, buy protection as financial conditions peak
bullets.body: Goldman's One-Delta desk advised staying in risk-on positioning, selling bonds, and purchasing protection, characterizing financial conditions as 'as loose as they get.' The desk separately warned that 'waging war is easier with stocks at all-time highs,' flagging geopolitical risk complacency. Hedge funds bought stocks every day last week, the second-fastest weekly buying pace of 2026.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz zero crossings; Iran shifts to offensive posture as 60-day truce expires
bullets.body: Hormuz tanker crossings returned to zero per Bloomberg, while Iran seized a UAE-owned tanker in the strait and officially shifted military policy from defensive to 'fully offensive,' setting a deadline of weeks for the US to implement an MOU. The 60-day US-Iran truce expired Monday without a final deal; Brent crude climbed ~3% to $90.74/bbl and WTI rose 2% to $84.14/bbl. The Pentagon reportedly has concluded no current military plan can guarantee safe Hormuz shipping, and the US Energy Secretary confirmed flows are running at only 8–9M bbl/day vs. normal capacity. The US SPR has fallen below 300M barrels, the lowest since January 1983.

bullets.title: China July data misses across the board; yuan at strongest since Feb 2023
bullets.body: China's July industrial production slowed to 4.5% YoY (below consensus), retail sales barely grew, and investment decline deepened—Goldman flagged downside risk to China's full-year growth. Simultaneously, the Chinese yuan strengthened to its highest level against the dollar since February 2023, and the dollar hit 2-month lows as the macro regime shifts away from July's Quad4 positioning.

bullets.title: Xi-Trump White House summit confirmed for Sept. 24; Xi skipping UN General Assembly
bullets.body: The White House confirmed Chinese President Xi Jinping will arrive in the US late September 23 and depart September 25, with a bilateral summit at the White House on September 24. Xi will skip the UN General Assembly, signaling the bilateral meeting is the primary diplomatic objective. Canada is also in 'intense, delicate' trade negotiations with the US, with more detail expected in the next 48 hours.

bullets.title: Copper near LME record on supply squeeze; backwardation widest since 2021
bullets.body: Copper spot traded $545/ton above three-month futures, the widest backwardation since 2021, as a near-term supply squeeze intensified driven by a surge in US-bound shipments ahead of potential tariffs. Global copper inventories are now heavily concentrated in the US. Aluminum rose 0.4% and zinc gained 0.3% on dollar weakness.

bullets.title: Global bond yields making multi-decade highs; Japan life insurers report record $96B unrealized losses
bullets.body: Alongside US 30y at 5.29%, France's 30y hit an 18-year high at 4.86%, Germany's 10y reached a 14-year high at 3.21%, and Japan's four largest life insurers reported a record $96B in unrealized domestic bond losses, surging $6B to all-time highs. Analysts attribute the long bond bear cycle to structural deficits and AI investment demand rather than Fed tightening alone.

bullets.title: Global debt issuance fell 16% YoY last week; IG corporate up 60%, leveraged loans collapsed 88%
bullets.body: Global debt issuance fell 16% YoY last week though YTD remains 9% above prior year. Investment-grade corporate issuance surged 60%, while high-yield fell 41% and leveraged loans plunged 88%—a sharp bifurcation signaling stress in lower-quality credit. Private credit portfolios are separately showing strain signals at 2017 levels per FT reporting.

bullets.title: Japan Q2 GDP misses (1.1% vs 2.0% est); traders price faster hikes in Japan, Canada, EU, UK vs US
bullets.body: Japan Q2 GDP grew just 1.1% annualized, missing the 2.0% consensus and decelerating from 2.1% prior. Separately, swap markets show traders pricing faster borrowing cost increases in Japan, Canada, the eurozone, and UK relative to the US over the next year, a notable divergence in rate trajectories.

bullets.title: Big tech has $3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments vs. $600B reported capex
bullets.body: Nine major tech companies have approximately $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI commitments—6x the $600B in reported capex—creating a large unrecognized obligation pool that investors may be systematically underestimating. Separately, AMD's $800M CapEx spend (vs. expected $200–300M) signals the traditional fabless model is eroding as chip designers secure scarce substrates and memory supply.

bullets.title: Unitree humanoid IPO massively oversubscribed (5,526–8,000x); implied opening at $41.66B vs $9B listing
bullets.body: Unitree, a Chinese humanoid robotics company, is set to IPO on the 19th with retail oversubscription of 5,526–8,000x, implying an opening market cap of ~$41.66B against a $9B IPO valuation—a 363% premium. The event is being read as a signal of genuine demand for humanoid robotics, with traders looking to US-listed names as proxies given restricted access to A-Shares.

bullets.title: Consumer stress signals: 1 in 3 Americans have no emergency savings; high-income households cutting essentials fastest
bullets.body: One-third of Americans report zero emergency savings per Empower, while high-income households are cutting spending on essential goods faster than lower-income households—an unusual bifurcation suggesting broad economic anxiety. Nearly 80% of Americans rate the economy poorly per ABC polling, even as the stock market hovers near all-time highs.

bullets.title: 75% of active managers underperformed S&P 500 over trailing 12 months; SPY +39% since Election Day 2024
bullets.body: 75% of active fund managers failed to beat the S&P 500 over the trailing 12 months. SPY is up 39% since Election Day 2024, while the rest-of-world index (CWI) has gained 50.5% over the same period—a notable divergence suggesting international equities have outperformed despite domestic investor focus.

bullets.title: Canada CPI hotter than expected at 3.0% YoY; Canada-US trade talks described as 'intense and delicate'
bullets.body: Canada's July CPI came in at 3.0% YoY, above the 2.9% consensus and 2.8% prior, with the MoM print at 0.5% vs. -0.4% prior. Separately, Canadian PM Carney characterized trade negotiations with the US as 'intense and delicate,' with Canadian trade officials meeting USTR Greer and Commerce in Washington; details expected within 48 hours.
